title: Are Personalized Stochastic Parrots More Dangerous? Evaluating Persona Biases in Dialogue Systems

bias_targets.methodology: Assigning gender-specific personas (e.g., woman, man, non-binary, transgender) to dialogue models and measuring variance in offensiveness, toxic continuation, regard, and stereotype agreement.
Assigning racial demographic personas and specific names associated with various countries to dialogue models, and evaluating changes in harmful expressions and agreements.
Assigning sexual orientation personas (e.g., gay, straight, pansexual, asexual) to dialogue models and measuring the sensitivity of harmful behaviors.
Assigning social class personas (e.g., lower class, middle class, upper class) to dialogue models and evaluating the variance in generated toxicity, offensiveness, and stereotype agreement.
Assigning education level personas (e.g., uneducated, high school, graduate) to dialogue models and measuring fluctuations in harmful expression and harmful agreement metrics.
Assigning generic and specific profession personas (e.g., doctor, plumber, artist) to dialogue models to evaluate the variance in their harmful behavior.
Assigning religious belief personas (e.g., Islam, Christianity, Atheism) to dialogue models and measuring changes in toxicity, offensiveness, and regard.
Assigning political ideology and specific political figure personas to dialogue models to evaluate how the harmfulness of their responses changes.
Assigning specific disability personas (e.g., musculoskeletal disorders, mental disorders) to dialogue models and evaluating the variance in harmfulness metrics.
